design_notes.note: The emission mechanism here is inrush, not switching. Turning the switch on charges the downstream capacitance from 0 V to VIN and the charge arrives as a current pulse: IRUSH = CL x SRON. With CL = 47 uF and the C-version slew rate, TI's worked example gives 150 mA of inrush -- a large, one-shot current step on a shared rail.

Slew rate, and therefore inrush amplitude, is chosen by ORDERING CODE, not by external components. The fast B version slews at 57 mV/us at 5 VIN (tON = 115 us); the slow C version is far gentler. Picking the C version is the datasheet's own remedy for inrush that would disturb the rail.
Input and output capacitors must sit close to the device so that parasitic trace inductance does not act on the switched current, and VIN, VOUT and GND traces must be wide and as short as possible.

TI's layout example deliberately routes the VOUT bypass capacitor ground and the device GND pin to system ground through a shared connection that forms a ground barrier, specifically to reduce the ground noise seen by the device.

provenance.notes: emissions.conducted[0] carries mechanism 'load_transient' with NO measurements. That is deliberate: the device has no oscillator and no switch node, so there is no f_fundamental_hz to record; its disturbance is a single inrush pulse whose amplitude is IRUSH = CL x SRON, i.e. a function of the downstream capacitance the designer chooses. The 150 mA figure in the design notes is TI's worked EXAMPLE at CL = 47 uF, not a device specification, so it was not stored as a measurement. No dissipation_model: the only power equation in the datasheet (Equation 5, page 20) computes the maximum ALLOWABLE dissipation from TJ, TA and theta_JA -- it is a limit, not an expression for actual dissipation, and storing it in dissipation_model would misrepresent it. Actual dissipation would be I_out^2 * RON using the RON table on page 5 (60 mOhm typ at 5 VIN, rising to 200 mOhm typ at 1 VIN), but that product is not written anywhere in the document so it was not invented. Package length/width come from the Device Information body size because the YFP0004 outline drawing labels D and E symbolically without numeric values. Page numbers are PDF page numbers, which coincide with the printed page numbers in this document.
